# Results summary: ESR1 structural diversity and redundancy

What the project did and found. Every number below is rendered from result files by
`scripts/collect_numbers_ext.py`; each finding names its figure (`figures/...`) and its result file (`results/...`).
All figures, with captions and sources: `docs/gallery.html` and `docs/figures/INDEX.md`. Methods: `docs/METHODOLOGY.md`.

## The data

- 901 ESR1 chains from the PDB; 788 chains from 351 entries pass the
  completeness screen and are all used (keep-all; 544 tier A, 240 tier B,
  4 tier C). All 351 entries are X-ray structures; 323 were grown with PEG;
  210 carry a co-crystallised peptide. Figure `figures/ext/Y02_metadata_overview.png`; file
  `results/ext/entry_metadata.csv`.
- Construct mutations are common: 443 chains carry Y537S and
  243 carry L536S; only 58 are wild type in the
  LBD (`results/ext/chain_metadata.csv`).

## 1. There are two conformations, and many methods agree

- Average linkage at 1.5 A gives 7 clusters: cl7
  (445 chains), cl4 (329) and five minor clusters (14 chains). The median RMSD
  between cl7 and cl4 is 3.49 A (`results/entry_clusters.csv`; `figures/ext/Y07_rmsd_heatmap_annotated.png`).
- All five embeddings separate the two (`figures/ext/Y03_embeddings.png`).
- Clustering zoo: 81 runs in 14 families. The declared rule selects spectral|sigma=2.0,k=2
  (silhouette 0.74, bootstrap stability 1.00, ARI with S08 0.94).
  The best runs of the top-7 families agree with S08 at ARI 0.89-0.98;
  density-based, medoid-based, single-linkage and affinity-propagation methods do not
  (`figures/ext/Y04_zoo_metrics.png`, `Y04_zoo_grid.png`, `Y06_agreement.png`, `Y06_alluvial.png`; `results/ext/zoo_runs.csv`).
- Compactness: cl7 mean pairwise RMSD 0.70 A (diameter 3.1 A), cl4
  0.91 A (diameter 2.4 A); cl4 is looser (`figures/ext/Y05_compactness.png`).
- Robustness: on core v3 and on the old core, every method in every subset (all, tier A, R-free <= 0.25, one chain
  per entry, complete H12) recovers the split with agreement 0.98-1.00
  (`figures/ext/Y28_robustness_grid.png`).
- Caveat found on the way (`figures/ext/Y42_metric_check.png`): the RMSD over pairwise-common positions is not a metric
  (5.4% of triples break the triangle inequality); chains without H12 look close
  to everyone. This is why PAM picked two H12-less chains as medoids.

## 2. Why two clusters: two positions of helix 12

- On H12 alone the median cl7-cl4 distance is 14.0 A; without residues 528-550 it is
  0.82 A and the clusters merge (`figures/ext/Y42_region_rmsd.png`). Positions 528-550 carry
  99% of the squared difference between the cluster means (`figures/ext/Y10_displacement_profile.png`).
- Geometry (`figures/ext/Y11_features_by_cluster.png`): H12 sits 12.3 A from its cl7 position in cl4
  (cl7 0.2 A); the H12-H3 axis angle is 82 vs 43 deg; the
  K362-E542 C-alpha distance is 19.3 vs 13.6 A. The two distributions do not overlap.
  This is the agonist (H12 capping the pocket, coactivator groove free) vs antagonist (H12 in the groove) geometry.
- Without any superposition, backbone dihedrals separate the clusters (silhouette 0.66); dihedral
  PC1 is essentially one residue, 537, the H11-H12 hinge (`figures/ext/Y12_phipsi_pca.png`).
- What decides the state (`figures/ext/Y13_feature_importance.png`, `Y14_split_hypotheses.png`):
  414 of 445 cl7 chains have a co-crystallised peptide vs 4 of
  329 cl4 chains (entry-level log odds ratio 6.7); Y537S (log OR 4.2) goes
  with cl7, L536S (log OR -6.7; 0 cl7 chains) with cl4; ligands with a basic amine go with
  cl4 (ligand-level log OR -5.3). Quality adds little once peptide and mutation are known (McFadden R2
  gain 0.053), and cl4 structures are, if anything, better (median resolution 1.88 vs
  2.22 A).
- Inside cl4, the 1.0 A sub-partition separates L536S constructs from the others; they differ at the H11-H12 loop
  (534, 533, 339) rather than H12 (`figures/ext/Y45_cl4_substructure.png`).

## 3. Outliers: quality or a different conformation?

- Five detectors flag 357 chains at least once; 22 chains (17 entries) are
  flagged by >= 3 (`figures/ext/Y15_outliers.png`).
- Consensus outliers are not worse in resolution, R-free, B or missing residues; 6 of
  22 have an individual quality reason, 16 look like real conformations. They differ
  in experimental conditions (fewer peptides, Y537S and P21 crystals) (`figures/ext/Y16_outlier_quality.png`;
  `results/ext/outlier_verdicts.csv`).
- Experimental metadata (`figures/ext/Y17_metadata_effects.png`): crystal form, construct and peptide track the
  cluster strongly; precipitant class, PEG, glycerol, DMSO and bound additives do not - the solvent does not explain
  the clusters. Crystallisation pH differs (median 8.3 vs 7.1), as part of the different
  crystal recipes.
- Crystal contacts at H12 (`figures/ext/Y44_h12_contacts.png`): median 1 lattice atoms touch H12
  in cl7 (the peptide sits there) vs 10 in cl4; in cl4 more contacts go with a fully ordered H12
  (17.5 vs 8.0) and a larger H12 shift (Spearman 0.55).
- Colour-by maps (`figures/ext/Y18_colour_by_quality.png`, `Y18_colour_by_experiment.png`, `Y18_colour_by_biology.png`,
  interactive `docs/interactive_embedding.html`) show the same thing visually.

## 4. B-factors and the alignment core

- The helix ranking by normalised B is the same in every B-group, cluster and tier; core v3 = the five most stable
  helices (338-362; 371-396; 420-439; 441-456; 496-531). Per chain, normalised B on core v3 is 0.93 vs
  1.04 on the old core (`figures/ext/Y21_helix_b.png`, `Y21_core_selection.png`).
- H12 is relatively more mobile in cl4 (H12 / core-v3 B ratio 1.53 vs
  1.33); PyMOL putty `figures/ext/Y30_pymol_bputty.png`.

## 5. Ligand chemistry and conformation

- Chemistry zoo: 276 runs; auto-selected MACCS|kmeans_mds|k=6 (K = 6, silhouette
  0.29, stability 0.97) after the declared rule's winner proved degenerate
  (`figures/ext/Y08_chem_zoo_metrics.png`, `Y08_chem_map.png`; C08 needs a human sign-off).
- Ligands of cl4 chains are larger (34 vs 24 heavy atoms, MW 470 vs
  344) and carry a basic amine far more often (74% vs 1%)
  (`figures/ext/Y09_physchem_by_cluster.png`, `Y09_scaffolds.png`).
- Chemistry and conformation are linked at the ligand level: permutation p 0.0001, Cramer's V
  0.43; 89% of ligands share the H12 state of their nearest chemical neighbour (null
  51%) (`figures/ext/Y25_chem_struct_link.png`, `Y25_nn_agreement.png`).
- cl4 ligands are more potent at ESR1 (+1.13 pChEMBL; +0.83 within chemistry
  clusters, p 0.02).

## 6. Redundancy: how many structures capture the diversity?

- Effective number of conformations (Hill q1): 2.19 at 1.5 A (q0 = 7 clusters);
  q1 stays about 2 for every method, core and subset (`figures/ext/Y26_hill_numbers.png`).
- Two complete-H12 representatives place 90% of all 788 chains within 1.0 A of one of them;
  at 0.5 A it takes 48 (`figures/ext/Y26_set_cover.png`). The earlier cluster-count definition needs
  488 random chains to see 90% of the 1.5 A clusters, because of rare singletons
  (`figures/ext/Y26_rarefaction.png`).
- Copies in one crystal differ by a median 0.54 A, the same ligand in another entry by
  0.65 A (`figures/ext/Y43_ncs_copies.png`).
- Time: since 2010 only 0.4% of new chains are > 1.5 A from every earlier one (median
  novelty 0.38 A); both states have existed since 1998
  (`figures/ext/Y27_timeline.png`, `Y27_novelty.png`).

## 7. ESR2

- ESR2 (86 chains, 39 entries) shows the same split: main basin
  93% peptide-bound, second basin 0% (`figures/ext/Y22_esr2_parallel.png`).
- In a joint frame, ESR2 agonist-state chains sit 1.33 A from ESR1 cl7, and the ESR2
  second basin 2.31 A from ESR1 cl4, while the two ESR1 states are
  3.49 A apart: the H12 state matters more than the receptor
  (`figures/ext/Y23_joint_embedding.png`). The draft pocket selectivity residues (384, 421) shift < 0.25 A in backbone
  (`figures/ext/Y23_receptor_residue_diff.png`).
- ChEMBL: 1615 compounds measured at both receptors, Spearman 0.50, 54%
  within 10-fold (`figures/ext/Y24_potency_esr1_vs_esr2.png`).
- The ESR2 reference could not meet core fraction 1.0 because ESR1 position 466 has no ESR2 counterpart; changing the
  reference does not change the ESR2 clusters (`docs/esr2_core_fraction.md`).

## Storyline: ten figures for the professor

1. **`figures/ext/Y07_rmsd_heatmap_annotated.png`** - The 788 x 788 RMSD matrix has two dark blocks.
   Everything that follows explains these two blocks.
2. **`figures/ext/Y04_zoo_grid.png`** - We tried 14 clustering families; the good ones all find the
   same two clusters. Density and medoid methods fail, and that failure taught us something about the distance itself.
3. **`figures/ext/Y05_compactness.png`** - Both clusters are tight (mean pairwise RMSD < 1 A) and far apart
   (3.5 A). cl7 is the more compact one.
4. **`figures/ext/Y10_displacement_profile.png`** - The difference sits in helix 12 and the loop before it
   (99% of it). Elsewhere only two poorly ordered loops move (up to 3.6 A).
5. **`figures/ext/Y30_pymol_medoids.png`** - In 3-D: H12 caps the ligand pocket in cl7 and lies in the coactivator groove
   in cl4. These are the classic agonist and antagonist conformations.
6. **`figures/ext/Y12_phipsi_pca.png`** - Even without any superposition, one backbone angle (residue 537) separates the
   clusters. The switch is a hinge, and residue 537 is where the Y537S construct mutation sits.
7. **`figures/ext/Y14_split_hypotheses.png`** - Coactivator peptide, Y537S vs L536S construct and a basic-amine ligand
   predict the cluster; quality does not. The experiment design decides which state a crystal shows.
8. **`figures/ext/Y16_outlier_quality.png`** - The odd structures are not the bad ones: only 6 of
   22 consensus outliers have a quality problem. Solvent and additives explain nothing
   (`figures/ext/Y17_metadata_effects.png`).
9. **`figures/ext/Y25_nn_agreement.png`** - Similar ligands give the same H12 state (89% vs
   51% by chance). Chemistry and conformation are linked.
10. **`figures/ext/Y26_set_cover.png`** - Two structures cover 90% of all chains at 1 A; the PDB holds about two
    effective conformations. Most of the 788 chains are repetition, and ESR2 repeats the same two states
    (`figures/ext/Y23_joint_embedding.png`).
